observation.visible_scene: Viewed through a transparent sheet, a blurred bearded man in safety glasses watches from the background. In the foreground a copper, gear/flower-shaped object is suspended by a metal clamp at the top, and a polished metal tube/rod enters from the right edge, its open end pointing left toward the gear. Water droplets and a splash pattern cling to the transparent sheet around the gear.
visible_changes: At the start the gear is ringed by a bright starburst of short radiating water jets, with elongated streaming droplets to the left; over the excerpt these jets shorten and retract, and the streaming shapes break into discrete round beads.
Water progressively accumulates as a beaded film on the gear teeth, so the gear looks increasingly wet and coated by the end, while the open starburst pattern largely disappears.
Scattered droplets on the sheet (notably the column of beads below the gear and the beads on the left) shift position, generally drifting downward within the frame.

The copper assembly drifts downward and slightly rightward relative to the man's face (gear center moves from upper-middle toward lower-middle), while the man's blurred face and the grassy background also shift downward, indicating a combined camera/scene drift rather than isolated gear motion.
The metal tube on the right stays roughly fixed relative to the right edge, pointing left, with only a small downward frame shift matching the overall drift.
More of the holder's upper body (a pale cylinder) enters the top of the frame toward the end, consistent with the downward drift of the scene.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the initial splash present at t=0 (the onset is before this excerpt).
Whether the metal tube is emitting anything or is merely positioned nearby.
What happens to the water and the gear after the excerpt ends.
uncertain_details: Whether the downward/rightward drift is camera motion, object motion, or both; background and subject shift together, so the split is not fully determinable.
Exact materials of the gear, clamp, tube, and the transparent sheet.
The man's precise gaze or expression due to heavy blur.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
